assessment.nobel_worthiness: Two-step defect-mediated melting with an intermediate hexatic phase is a textbook case of a simple, universal mechanism (dislocation and disclination unbinding, with RG flows and universal exponents) explaining a messy phenomenon. It is original, mathematically clean, and has shaped soft matter, liquid crystals, colloids, vortex lattices and graphene physics. Its importance is high and its mechanism well understood.
assessment.attribution: The topological-defect framework was recognized in 2016 (Kosterlitz, Thouless, Haldane). The hexatic extension is the decisive step credited to Halperin and Nelson, with Young's independent dislocation-mediated melting and scaling work. Halperin, Nelson and Young is a fair, compact trio that complements the 2016 prize; I am not certain of every priority detail and the committee may worry about overlap with 2016.
assessment.maturity: Mature for decades: the hexatic phase has been seen in colloids, in simulations (after long debate over first-order versus continuous scenarios) and in 2D materials. Interpretation is stable, and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize may make the Academy hesitant.
Details of the order of melting (continuous vs weakly first-order) remain system dependent.
Fine priority among Halperin-Nelson and Young is from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and stochastic thermodynamics extend the second law to individual trajectories of small, driven, far-from-equilibrium systems with exact results. This is nonequilibrium statistical mechanics of the kind I trust: a clean general relation, now used from single-molecule biophysics to colloids and quantum devices. It has changed how thermodynamics is applied at the nanoscale.
assessment.attribution: Evans and collaborators gave the first fluctuation relations for driven systems, Jarzynski the equality linking work to free energy, Crooks the detailed fluctuation relation, and Seifert the trajectory-level stochastic thermodynamics framework. A three-person prize is workable but forces a hard choice; I select Jarzynski, Evans, Seifert while acknowledging Crooks' strong claim, and that Gallavotti-Cohen and others are not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by single-molecule pulling experiments (RNA, proteins) and by colloidal and electronic realizations; the theory is mature and widely taught. Timing is reasonable, though the field's identity as a single discovery is somewhat diffuse.
uncertainties: Credit is spread over more than three people and over earlier work outside the credited list.
The dominant experimental confirmations are of a theory-led picture, so the prize would be primarily theoretical.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory solved the infinite-dimension limit of correlated lattice models by mapping them to a self-consistent quantum impurity problem. It supplied a controlled, conceptually simple framework for the Mott transition and for realistic materials via DFT+DMFT. It is the central non-perturbative tool for strongly correlated electrons.
assessment.attribution: The infinite-dimension limit is due to Metzner and Vollhardt, with the DMFT mapping by Georges and Kotliar (and Müller-Hartmann and others). The supplied trio is defensible but leaves out Metzner, which I flag as an attribution issue; I propose the three credited.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with thirty years of use, comparison with cluster extensions, cold-atom checks and quantitative material predictions. Recognition is timely. Success is in understanding mechanisms such as Mott physics rather than a single decisive experiment.
uncertainties: Omission of Metzner and Müller-Hartmann in the credit set.
A tool rather than a discovery may be a hurdle for a Physics Prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene turned a simple moiré continuum model into a flat-band platform with correlated insulators and superconductivity. The Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction of a magic angle followed by an experimental discovery is a clear theory-experiment story, and it opened a large field of moiré materials. The significance is high and rising.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted flat bands near 1.1 degrees; Jarillo-Herrero's group observed correlated insulators and superconductivity. Cao and others on the experimental paper are not in the credited names, so a fair configuration is hard. The three supplied names cover prediction and experiment well.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, with robust phenomenology; the origin of the superconductivity is still debated. This is slightly early for a final verdict on mechanism but the discovery is solid.
uncertainties: Experimental credit includes junior authors not in the credited set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains flatness, horizon uniformity and the seed spectrum of structure via quantum fluctuations, and its predictions on near-scale-invariant adiabatic perturbations have matched CMB data. It is one of the most consequential ideas in modern cosmology and is conceptually very economical.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed the scenario, Linde (new inflation, chaotic) made it viable, and Mukhanov computed quantum-origin fluctuations. Starobinsky and Albrecht-Steinhardt also had decisive roles and are not among the credited names, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong CMB support for the perturbation features, but no direct detection of primordial gravitational waves and many competing inflation models. Recognition could be seen as premature in direct-test terms.
uncertainties: No primordial B-mode detection and ongoing model degeneracy.
Credit disputes (Starobinsky, Sato and others outside the credited list).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recognition that particles in two dimensions can have fractional statistics is a deep general idea tied to topology and underlies fractional quantum Hall quasiparticles and topological quantum computing. Experimental braiding signatures in interferometers and collider geometries now make it an observed phenomenon.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim made the theoretical identification, with Wilczek's anyon naming not credited here, while Heiblum, Fève, Manfra and Rosenow cover experiment and theory of quasiparticle statistics. The six names forces a hard three-person choice; I choose the theory pair plus Heiblum for the experimental establishment.
assessment.maturity: Experiments of 2020 onwards are recent and the interpretation continues to be refined; independent reproduction is increasing. The timing is borderline.
uncertainties: Large credit set and omitted central figures such as Wilczek.
Interferometer interpretation subtleties (Coulomb effects) are still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy-landscape theory with minimal frustration explains how heteropolymers fold quickly using ideas from spin glasses and random-energy models. It is a clean statistical-mechanics resolution of Levinthal's paradox that guides simulation and interpretation. I value it as a physics-style mechanism for a biological problem.
assessment.attribution: Bryngelson and Wolynes introduced the spin-glass approach, with Onuchic and Wolynes developing the funnel landscape. The supplied trio is consistent with this history.
assessment.maturity: Widely used and consistent with experiments, but its status as primarily physical versus chemical/biological discovery is uncertain, and the AlphaFold-era work does not replace its conceptual role.
uncertainties: May be better suited for Chemistry or Physiology rather than Physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Emergent magnetic monopoles in spin ice are a striking example of fractionalized excitations and emergent gauge structure with a simple dumbbell/Coulomb description. It links frustrated magnetism with gauge theory and has been probed by thermodynamics, neutron scattering and noise.
assessment.attribution: Castelnovo, Moessner and Sondhi proposed the emergent monopole picture; experimental groups (Bramwell, Morris, Fennell) are not in the credited set, so an experimentally grounded configuration is awkward.
assessment.maturity: Observation is indirect and some interpretations remain debated, so maturity is moderate. It is still a field with active development.
uncertainties: Evidence is indirect and less definitive than for a fundamental discovery.
